solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Son tucked into much loved duck and Italian sauce (5)

indicatorNotes.tucked into: the son is tucked inside the pet, as a child into bed

blocks.note: a pet is a much-loved favourite
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

annotation.surface: A menu: duck served with an Italian sauce, and a son happily tucking in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the meat course, but it is the cricketer's zero. S goes inside PET, and O is added at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Pesto is the basil-and-pine-nut sauce from Genoa.

entries.clue: Country’s body of water containing algae regularly avoided (6)

indicatorNotes.containing: the pond holds the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.regularly avoided: every other letter of 'algae' is skipped, keeping L and A

blocks.note: a pond is a small body of water
skip A, G and E in a-L-g-A-e, leaving L and A

annotation.surface: A nation's lake kept clear of pond scum.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', linking the country to the wordplay. LA sits between PO and ND.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Poland is one country among many in central Europe.

entries.clue: Disease’s evidence of harm felt wrong always (7,5)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters of 'felt' are put the wrong way round

blocks.note: a scar is the mark an injury leaves

annotation.surface: A patient describing a disease: visible damage, and it always felt wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' and links the definition to the wordplay. 'Felt' looks like a verb about feeling ill, but it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is a bacterial infection with a red rash, mostly in children.

entries.clue: In public view, Dicky rides unfancied racehorse (8)

indicatorNotes.Dicky: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of 'rides' are out of order

blocks.note: something that is out is openly known

annotation.surface: A jockey named Dicky riding a long shot where everyone can see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a jockey's name; it is the British adjective for shaky or unsound, used here to mix up RIDES.
annotation.definitionFit: An outsider is a horse given little chance of winning.

entries.clue: Peculiar drink raised commotion (6)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it bottom to top

blocks.note: rum = odd, in old-fashioned British speech

annotation.surface: A strange drink stirred up a fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar drink' reads as one phrase, suggesting rum as the drink itself; in fact 'Peculiar' gives RUM and 'drink' gives SUP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean a noisy fuss or uproar.

entries.clue: Initially, Ben uncovers Rolls Royce’s humming sound (4)

indicatorNotes.Initially: take the first letters of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of Ben and uncovers
RR is the badge of Rolls-Royce

annotation.surface: Ben pulls off a car cover to reveal a purring Rolls-Royce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovers' looks like the verb of the scene, but it only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A burr is a low whirring or humming noise.

entries.clue: Picked up this writer covering part of Observer? (6)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

annotation.surface: A journalist spotted writing for part of the Observer newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, but here it is just anyone who observes, whose eyelid is part of them; the question mark flags the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: An eyelid is part of the eye of whoever is looking.

entries.clue: French one meets American university supporter rarely (9)

annotation.surface: A Frenchman seldom meets a fan of an American college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American university' looks like one phrase, perhaps a college name, but splits into US and U.
annotation.definitionFit: Unusually and rarely both mean not often, in 'not unusually cold'.

entries.clue: Canadian singer-songwriter played chord alone, half seen (7,5)

indicatorNotes.played: the letters are played around with, like notes
indicatorNotes.half: only one half of 'seen' is used

annotation.surface: A singer-songwriter strums a single chord on stage, half in view.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface fits the answer neatly: 'played' and 'chord' are just what Leonard Cohen did, which disguises the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Leonard Cohen was the Canadian writer of 'Hallelujah' and 'Suzanne'.

entries.clue: Jumped as plate smashed (5)

indicatorNotes.smashed: the plate breaks and its letters are pieced together differently

annotation.surface: Someone jumped at the sound of a plate smashing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain scene of alarm, so 'smashed' reads as what happened to the plate rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Leapt is a past tense of leap, to jump.

entries.clue: Fantastic winger’s big match in US (5,4)

blocks.note: a winger here is a bird

annotation.surface: A brilliant footballer on the wing plays in a big American game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winger' is a wide player in football, but here anything with wings; the obvious break after SUPER is the wrong one.
annotation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the championship game of American football.

entries.clue: Outstanding musical performance of couple shortened (3)

indicatorNotes.shortened: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a duet is a piece for two performers

annotation.surface: Praise for a superb duet that was cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the performance, but it means unpaid, as a bill is outstanding.
annotation.definitionFit: The money sense: a bill still unpaid is both outstanding and owed.

entries.clue: Panel of vehicle mum found in terribly bad road (9)

indicatorNotes.found in: the silencing word sits inside the others
indicatorNotes.terribly: the letters of 'bad road' are badly jumbled

blocks.note: mum = silent, as in 'keep mum'; SH asks for quiet

annotation.surface: A car's instrument panel goes quiet on a rough road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, the usual MA, but here it means silent, as in 'keep mum'.
annotation.definitionFit: The dashboard is the panel of instruments in front of a driver.

entries.clue: Giant winged insect under hebe fluttered (8)

indicatorNotes.fluttered: the letters of 'hebe' flap about into a new order
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, the moth goes below the other part

blocks.note: a moth is a winged insect

annotation.surface: A huge moth flutters beneath a hebe bush in the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: A hebe is a common garden shrub, which makes 'fluttered' look like the moth's movement rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A behemoth is something enormous, from the biblical beast.

entries.clue: Do a makeover on hair and blunder (9)

blocks.note: bish is British slang for a mistake

annotation.surface: A hairdresser gives a makeover and makes a mess of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On hair' reads as the makeover's target, but 'on' is RE. Bish is an informal British word for a blunder.
annotation.definitionFit: Renovating a room or building gives it a makeover, the property sense of the word.

entries.clue: Florid Australian native going round business clubs (6)

indicatorNotes.going round: the kangaroo's letters surround the others

annotation.surface: A flamboyant Australian doing the rounds of business clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests an Aborigine, but it is the kangaroo; CO and C sit inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Rococo is the highly ornate 18th-century style, so florid.

entries.clue: Single working Scotsman related to Ancient Greeks (6)

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working
Ian is the Scottish form of John

annotation.surface: An unmarried Scot in work who is descended from the Greeks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single' reads as unmarried, but it is the numeral I.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ionians were one of the main tribes of ancient Greece.

entries.clue: Hideout finally had more protection (3)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: last letters of haD, morE, protectioN

annotation.surface: A hideout that at last offered better shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' reads as 'at last' in the story, which hides that it applies to each of the three words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A den is a secret hiding place.

entries.clue: Knight in charge, see, in a pleasant way (6)

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in England

annotation.surface: A knight in command courteously invites someone to look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb, but it is a bishop's diocese; Ely is the one crosswords use most.
annotation.definitionFit: The adverb of nice, so the definition is an adverbial phrase of the same meaning.

entries.clue: Beware of dog with stick originally muzzled behind hole in rock (4,5)

indicatorNotes.behind: the stick and M come after the cave

blocks.note: a cave is a hollow in rock
a cane is a walking stick

annotation.surface: A dog warning: the animal is muzzled and kept in a cave with a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog-themed surface (muzzled, stick) fits the answer, the Latin warning found in a Pompeii mosaic.
annotation.definitionFit: Cave canem is Latin for 'beware of the dog'.

entries.clue: Imbecile Conservative group (4)

blocks.note: a lot is a group or batch

annotation.surface: A jibe calling a Tory faction idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: Clot is a mild British insult for a foolish person.
annotation.definitionFit: A mild British insult for a stupid person, so a synonym in everyday slang.

entries.clue: Brownish-yellow brooch restored somewhat (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the words' letters are used

annotation.surface: A tarnished brooch, partly restored to a yellowish-brown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Restored' looks like a signal to rearrange, but the letters run in order across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: The name of an earth pigment, and hence of its colour.

entries.clue: Motor car crashed trapping northern seabird (9)

indicatorNotes.crashed: the motor car's letters are wrecked into a new order
indicatorNotes.trapping: the rearranged letters hold N inside

annotation.surface: A car crash on a northern road pins a seabird.
annotation.walkthrough: N goes in before the final T.
annotation.definitionFit: A cormorant is a large dark diving seabird.

entries.clue: Harry’s outside hugging somebody dear (5)

indicatorNotes.outside: only the outer letters of Harry are kept
indicatorNotes.hugging: the outer letters wrap round the other word

blocks.note: first and last letters of Harry
one = someone, as in 'one never knows'

annotation.surface: Harry is outdoors embracing a loved one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry's outside' reads as 'Harry is outdoors', but it means Harry's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Honey and dear are both terms of endearment.
